citations.description: Ticket comment (timestamp 1786139466408095001): 'AC#1 (the hanging test/blocking call is named with a log line or repro showing it stalled) — operator-attested. The specific test was never captured off-runner (does not reproduce locally) and, since the guard merged, the hang has not recurred under normal contention (it was Actions-outage-adjacent), so the guard has not needed to fire to name it. The committed compensating control (per-test 300s thread-method timeout + pytest-timeout) guarantees any recurrence self-names instead of going silent, which is the operational intent. Operator attests this satisfies AC#1.'

findings.criterion: [operator-attested] the hanging test (or the blocking call) is named, with a CI log line or a local reproduction showing it stalled
findings.detail: The operator attestation in the ticket's third comment explicitly states: 'The specific test was never captured off-runner (does not reproduce locally) and, since the guard merged, the hang has not recurred under normal contention... so the guard has not needed to fire to name it.' The criterion requires the hanging test or blocking call to be named with a CI log line or local reproduction showing it stalled. The attestation does not provide a specific test name, a CI log line showing a stall, or a local reproduction — it instead argues the compensating control (per-test timeout) satisfies the criterion by ensuring a future recurrence will self-name. An assertion that a future recurrence will name itself is not the same as the hanging test having been named. The criterion's concrete requirement (name the test, with a log line or repro) is not met by the attestation.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment that names the specific hanging test (or blocking call site) with either: (a) a CI log line from a run where the per-test timeout fired and named the test, or (b) a local reproduction showing the specific test stalling. The compensating control is in place; the next recurrence should produce this evidence automatically — capture it and record it here.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify.
